firing.source: type A = { readonly a: number }; type B = { readonly b: number }; declare const either: A | B; const a = either as A;

findings.message: 'A | B' can't be cast to 'A' here: nothing at runtime could confirm it, so the cast is trusted, not proven, and every use after it inherits the guess. Return or declare 'A' where the value comes from, or build one from fields you have narrowed with typeof. A cast from a union to some of its members is allowed when a discriminant property, typeof or instanceof can tell them apart, since Adamic compiles that to a check.
